figures.caption: Figure 1: Transformation of loss landscape geometry. Standard optimisation assumes a flat Euclidean space (left). By defining the metric tensor gϕ and minimising distances under the induced geometry, optimisation moves into non-Euclidean spaces. The resulting trajectories are illustrated for Riemannian (center) and hyperbolic (right) geometries, showing how learned geometric mappings reshape optimisation paths and improve stability.

Figure 2: Geometry-aware distillation. Teacher and student representations are projected into a shared manifold space, where alignment is performed through geodesic optimization while KL divergence preserves output consistency.

Table 2: Evaluation metric definitions and reporting conventions used throughout Sec. 4. “Direction” indicates whether higher (↑) or lower (↓) values are preferred. WER and CER are reported in percentage points; RTFx is unitless; parameter and memory counts are in MB.

Table 3: Comparison with Whisper baselines and Distil-Whisper on the LibriSpeech test splits. “Train data” is the audio duration used for distillation training. Lower WER and higher RTFx are better indications. Numbers for Whisper and Distil-Whisper baselines are taken from [Radford et al., 2023] and [Gandhi et al., 2023]. RC results are obtained on a single H200 GPU under the protocol of Sec. 4.2.
